concepts.title: Meaning of Financial Statement Analysis
concepts.definition: Financial statement analysis is the systematic study of the figures inside a company's statements -- sorting, relating and reading them -- so that the profitability, efficiency and health of the firm can be judged and decisions taken.
concepts.key_idea: Analysis simplifies the raw data first; interpretation then turns the simplified figures into judgements about the firm.

solution_steps.explain: methodical classification of the statement figures reduces a mass of numbers to workable groups
items are compared across time, across statements and against totals to expose patterns
the relationships are interpreted to judge profitability, operational efficiency and financial health

concepts.title: Significance of Financial Statement Analysis
concepts.definition: By setting statement items side by side, analysis exposes the strengths and weaknesses of a firm, and each reader -- management inside, creditors, investors and government outside -- extracts the answer to its own question.
concepts.key_idea: The same analysed numbers let management steer, lenders secure and investors choose.

solution_steps.explain: management measures efficiency, spots weaknesses and plans corrections

concepts.title: Objectives of Financial Statement Analysis
concepts.definition: Analysis aims at judging the earning capacity and efficiency of the firm, testing its ability to meet short-term and long-term obligations, and enabling comparison of performance across years and across firms.
concepts.key_idea: Every objective reduces to one move: put two figures beside each other and ask what the gap means.

concepts.title: Tools of Financial Analysis
concepts.definition: The analyst's toolkit holds comparative statements, common size statements, trend analysis, ratio analysis and cash flow analysis; the first two run side by side (horizontal) while common size percentages read down the statement (vertical).
concepts.formula: toolkit = comparative_statements + common_size_statements + trend_analysis + ratio_analysis + cash_flow_analysis
concepts.key_idea: Comparative work is horizontal analysis across periods; common size work is vertical analysis inside one period.

solution_steps.explain: comparative statements set two years' absolute figures and changes together; trend percentages stretch the view over several years
common size statements express each item as a percentage of a common base; ratios relate chosen pairs of figures
cash flow analysis traces where funds came from and where they went

concepts.title: Trend Percentage
concepts.definition: A trend percentage shows how each item of a chosen year stands against the same item of a fixed base year, with the base year itself read as one hundred.
concepts.key_idea: One fixed base year turns scattered yearly figures into a long-run direction line for every item.

concepts.title: Comparative Statement: Absolute Change
concepts.definition: In a comparative statement the change column is found by subtracting each previous year figure from the matching current year figure, and the result is read as an increase or a decrease in rupees.
concepts.key_idea: A positive difference is an increase shown with a plus sign; a negative one is a decrease shown with a minus sign.

concepts.title: Comparative Statement: Percentage Change
concepts.definition: The percentage column of a comparative statement divides the absolute change by the first year figure and multiplies by one hundred, showing how fast the item moved relative to where it started.
concepts.key_idea: Rupees say how much moved; the percentage says how big the move was against the base, which is what makes years comparable.

concepts.title: Profit after Tax in a Comparative Statement
concepts.definition: Each year's column in a comparative profit statement runs from total revenue, through expenses, to profit before tax, then tax at that year's rate, and finally profit after tax -- and the change columns compare the two years' bottom lines.
concepts.key_idea: Tax belongs inside each year's column, so both the absolute and percentage comparisons of profit after tax are fair.

concepts.title: Common Size Statement Percentage
concepts.definition: A common size statement re-expresses every item as a percentage of one chosen base for the same period -- revenue from operations in the profit statement, total assets or total liabilities in the balance sheet.
concepts.key_idea: Because every item becomes a share of the same hundred, statements of firms of very different sizes become comparable.

concepts.title: Inter-firm Use of Common Size Analysis
concepts.definition: Stripping out absolute sizes, common size percentages let an analyst compare the structure of statements of firms of different magnitudes in one industry, and track how one firm's structure shifts year after year.
concepts.key_idea: Percentages kill the size advantage: a small firm and a giant can be read on the same page.
question_patterns: why are common size statements suited to comparing firms of different sizes

solution_steps.explain: each item becomes a share of the common base, so absolute size stops mattering
cost shares, asset mixes and financing patterns line up side by side
the same statement over successive years shows which components grew or shrank in importance

concepts.title: Limitations of Financial Analysis
concepts.definition: Analysis inherits every weakness of the statements behind it: it ignores price level changes, stumbles on undisclosed accounting policy changes, reads only monetary data, and studies past reports rather than live conditions.
concepts.key_idea: Windows dressed for presentation and personal judgement inside the figures pass straight through into every tool's output.

solution_steps.explain: whatever weakened the statements -- estimates, conventions, judgements -- weakens the analysis

solution_steps.action: flag the price level blind spot
solution_steps.explain: figures of different years sit on different price levels, so raw comparisons mislead
non-monetary aspects stay invisible, and policy changes or window dressing can bend every ratio and percentage
